record.paper_title: Open Problems Related to Quantum Query Complexity
record.context_brief: Approximate degree versus quantum query complexity for partial functions
record.original_question: For a partial Boolean function f:S->{0,1}, where S is a subset of {0,1}^n, let the approximate degree of f be the minimum degree of a real polynomial p:R^n->R such that |p(x)-f(x)|<=1/3 for every promised input x in S and p(x) lies in [0,1] for every Boolean input x in {0,1}^n. What is the largest possible gap between the bounded-error quantum query complexity Q(f) and the approximate degree of f? Can this gap be exponential?

evidence.quote: Let f : S→{ 0, 1} be a partial Boolean function, where S⊆{ 0, 1}n. Define the approximate degree of f, or ˜deg (f), to be the minimum degree of a real polynomial p : Rn→ R such that (i) |p (x)− f (x)|≤ 1/3 for all x∈ S, and (ii) p (x)∈ [0, 1] for all x∈{ 0, 1}n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and let S ⊆ {0,1}^n. A partial Boolean function is a map f : S → {0,1}. 

Define the approximate degree of f, denoted deg̃(f), to be the minimum nonnegative integer d such that there exists a real polynomial p : R^n → R of degree at most d satisfying:
  (i) |p(x) − f(x)| ≤ 1/3 for every x ∈ S, and
  (ii) p(x) ∈ [0,1] for every x ∈ {0,1}^n.

Let Q(f) denote the bounded-error quantum query complexity of f, i.e., the minimum number of quantum oracle queries required by a quantum algorithm that, on every input x ∈ S, outputs f(x) with probability at least 2/3.

It is known that deg̃(f) ≤ O(Q(f)) for every partial Boolean function f. Determine the largest possible asymptotic gap between Q(f) and deg̃(f) over all partial Boolean functions f : S → {0,1} with S ⊆ {0,1}^n. In particular, can this gap be exponential? That is, does there exist a family of partial Boolean functions for which Q(f) is exponentially larger than deg̃(f)?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Ambainis–Belovs, CCC 2023) established an exponential separation between exact polynomial degree and bounded-error quantum query complexity for partial Boolean functions, but this concerns exact degree rather than approximate degree. The analogous question for approximate degree—whether Q(f) can be exponentially larger than deg̃(f) for partial f—does not appear to be resolved in the located literature, and remains listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: An Exponential Separation Between Quantum Query Complexity and the Polynomial Degree
status_evidence.snippet: we demonstrate an exponential separation between exact polynomial degree and approximate quantum query complexity for a partial Boolean function
status_evidence.claim: A separation is known for exact degree vs Q on partial functions, but this is distinct from the approximate-degree question.

status_evidence.title: An Exponential Separation Between Quantum Query Complexity and the Polynomial Degree (journal version)
status_evidence.snippet: there is at most a polynomial separation between quantum query complexity and the polynomial degree for total functions; the precise relationship between the two is not clear for partial functions
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the partial-function relationship between Q and degree measures is still an active open area.
